layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Solutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The electrochemical response of Al alloys containing various concentrations of Mo in solid solution was studied using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentiodynamic polarization. The evolution of the chemical composition of the passive film during exposure to deaerated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.1N KCl was analyzed using x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Exposure of Al-Mo alloys to the chloride solution results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in an increase in the corrosion potential and a decrease in the cathodic Tafel slope. The breakdown potential is also found

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to increase with higher concentrations of Mo in the alloy. These results correlate with an increase in the amount of Mo in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the oxide film during polarization, even though the concentration of Mo in the passive film is well below that in the alloy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This work suggests that the oxidized Mo in the passive film inhibits the nucleation of pits in the alloy by improving the in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tegrity of the passive film.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Aluminum is a reactive metal that owes its resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to environmental attack to the formation of an inert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive film on its surface. The rate that the passive film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dissolves in aqueous solutions controls the general cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rosion characteristics of the metal. Between pH 4 and 9,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the solubility of the passive film decreases and protects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the metal substrate from attack (1). Away from near-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neutral pH conditions, the solubility of the film and,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: therefore, the general corrosion rate of the metal in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creases (2, 3).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The presence of certain aggressive anions in the solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, most notably chlorides, results in the localized at-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tack of the passive film. The pits that form during the at-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tack are caused by an accelerated dissolution of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive film and of the metal substrate. This, in turn,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leads to locally high current densities and changes in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution chemistry inside the pit. The pitting process in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volves a series of reaction steps including the adsorption

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the Cl- anion and its chemical interaction with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive film and subsequent thinning of the film fol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowed by the exposure and rapid dissolution of the metal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: substrate (4). The overall process can be effectively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: controlled in aluminum through the use of inhibitors,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as either molybdates, chromates, or nitrates (5, 6),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the solution. The mechanism by which the corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inhibitor improves the integrity of the passive film is not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clearly understood. Results of analyses of the interaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of inhibitors with aluminum using x-ray photoelectron

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spectroscopy (XPS) and Rutherford backscattering

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spectroscopy (RBS) indicate that the inhibitor anion is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incorporated into the passive film during exposure to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution (7-9). The common characteristic of these inhibi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tors and their interaction with the passive film is that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their chemical state, as measured by XPS, is reduced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the higher valence state in the inhibitor during the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incorporation of the species into the passive film. In the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: case of the molybdate inhibitor, two chemical states,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo+⁶ and Mo+4, were detected (7, 8). It was suggested that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the inhibiting effect may be due to molybdate adsorp-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, reduction, and inclusion in the passive film, thereby

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improving the film's resistance to local attack, possibly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by blocking paths used by the Cl- anion to reach the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oxide/metal interface.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To determine whether reduction of the ion is essential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to improving the passivity of Al exposed to chloride so-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lutions, we directly alloyed Mo to Al to eliminate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presence of the higher Mo valence state

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , thereby

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: removing the reduction step from the inhibiting process.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Because the solid solubility of Mo in Al is very low, ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forts to eliminate pitting by its addition to Al using a con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ventional ingot metallurgy approach have been unsuc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cessful. Addition of Mo to Al generally leads to the pref-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erential nucleation of pits at the precipitates in the alloy,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the pitting resistance of the material is diminished

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from that of the pure metal. Recently, Mo has been di-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rectly alloyed to Al using ion implantation (10, 11) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: RF-magnetron sputter-deposition (12). Both techniques

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: allow the Mo to be retained in solid solution with the Al

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at concentrations well above its solubility limit in Al

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without the formation of Mo-rich precipitates (12, 13).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The resistance of these Al-Mo alloys to pitting attack is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: substantially increased. Figure 1 shows the effect that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adding 6 atom percent (a/o) Mo to an Al sputter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deposited film has on the pitting potential, as measured

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentiodynamically (12). The same concentration of Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was even sufficient to passivate the alloy when it was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tested in air-saturated chloride solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results of the polarization behavior of the alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing Mo in solid solution with Al are similar to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests on pure Al conducted in aqueous solutions con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taining molybdates, where pitting potentials as high as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: +1V, with respect to the saturated calomel electrode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (SCE), have been reported (6), and the resistance of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: material to localized attack is increased significantly.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The improvement in the ability of the passive film to re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sist localized attack in each case suggests a similar mech-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anism for Mo interaction with the passive film. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the passive flm that forms when an Al-Mo alloy is ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed to an aggressive chloride-containing electrolyte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: must evolve through a series of steps that are likely to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quite different than those occurring when Al is exposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to a molybdate inhibitor. Understanding the nature of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the evolution of the passive film in either system, in re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sponse to the exposure of Al to chloride-containing solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions, is essential in isolating the key elements that play a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: role in improving resistance to localized attack.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this investigation, the response of Al alloys con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taining various concentrations of Mo in solid solution to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anodic and cathodic potentiodynamic polarization has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been used to characterize the corrosion behavior of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: material in 0.1N KCl. The evolution in the surface chem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: istry of the passive film as a result of changes in the elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trochemistry of the system have been analyzed, using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: XPS and high-resolution scanning electron microscopy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (HSEM). The results of this work are discussed in light of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the molybdate-inhibited Al system.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Experimental Procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Specimen preparation.—Metal films of Al alloyed with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various concentrations of Mo were prepared by co-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depositing the two elements onto a 5 cm diam single-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crystal silicon wafer, using the RF magnetron sputter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deposition process. This process involves using two sep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: arate Al and Mo targets to grow films at a rate of 5 Å/s.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The vacuum pressure in the chamber prior to sputtering

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was 10-7 torr. Immediately after the start of sputter depo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sition, the silicon was cooled to near -196°C to minimize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heating the alloy during sputtering and suppress the for-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mation of Mo-rich precipitates. The films were not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cooled before sputter deposition to avoid using the wafer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a cold finger and increasing contamination of the sur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: face. Between 0.8 and 1.0 μm of the Al-Mo alloy was de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posited onto the Si. After deposition, the temperature of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the alloy increased slowly to ambient prior to its removal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the vacuum chamber.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The composition of the film was controlled by setting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Al target to the maximum power and varying the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: power to the Mo target. Because the targets were close to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Si, the composition of the alloy varied across the wa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fer. Specimens used for this study were taken from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: center of the wafer, where the compositional and thick-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ness gradients were the lowest. The center of the wafer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was separated into eight sections by cleaving the silicon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: along lines scribed onto its rear surface. Sections of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flms that were scratched during handling were not used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the polarization tests. The average Mo composition in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each area of the film was determined on a duplicate sam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ple by dissolving the alloy off of the Si, measuring the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: weight loss, and determining the concentration of Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Al in thę solvent. This information was compared

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the results of the XPS analysis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Electron microscopy and x-ray diffraction.—The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HSEM was performed on a JEOL 100 CX at 40 kV on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sample surface in both the as-sputtered condition and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: after exposure to the electrolyte following polarization.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The samples were coated with a thin layer of platinum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prior to analysis, in order to reduce charging of the sur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: face. Specimens were prepared for transmission electron

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: microscopy (TEM) by polishing the back side of the sili-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: con until the final thickness of the wafer was close to 50

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: μm. A copper-rhodium mask with an oval hole was then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: glued to the polished silicon side with epoxy. An area

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thin enough for transmission of a 100 kV beam was made

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by ion milling the Si side with argon on a Gatan Model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 600 ion miller at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 3 kV until perforation. The sam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ple was milled on a cold stage to prevent heating during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thinning.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The presence of precipitates in the films was deter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mined using selected area diffraction (SAD), as well as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: glancing angle x-ray diffraction (XRD). The SAD pat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: terns were made at 100 kV. The glancing angle XRD was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performed on a Siemens diffractometer using a mono-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromatic Cu

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: x-ray source. The angle between the in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cident x-rays and the specimen was held constant at 12°,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while the detector for the diffracted x-rays was swept in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an arc around the sample. This technique improved the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signal-to-noise of the as-deposited Al-Mo film over con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ventional diffraction techniques by at least 50%, and also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eliminated diffraction from the silicon substrate.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Electrochemical polarization measurements.—Each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polarized sample was masked with lacquer and allowed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to dry for 24h. The electrolyte used in this study was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: made by mixing 500 ml distilled water with reagent-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grade KCl to obtain a solution of 0.1N KCl. The electro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lyte was first degassed under vacuum and subsequently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deaerated with high purity nitrogen. The pH of the solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion was adjusted to 8 with KOH. The electrode was held

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the middle of the flask and a magnetic stirrer was used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to vigorously agitate the solution throughout the test.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The samples were placed into the electrolyte and al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowed to come to an equilibrium corrosion potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Ecor®) prior to polarization. The potential was monitored

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: continuously after immersion and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was determined

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when the change in the open-circuit potential was less

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than 1 mV over a 6 min period. A platinum wire mesh

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a surface area at least ten times that of the working

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrode was used as a counterelectrode. An SCE, used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a reference electrode, was held approximately 2 mm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the surface of the working electrode, using a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Luggin probe. Potentiodynamic polarization measure-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments were performed with a Princeton Applied Re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: search PAR Model 273 potentiostat/galvanostat by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scanning anodically or cathodically from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at 0.2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mV/s.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Surface analysis.—Samples to be analyzed by XPS

layout_dets.text: The results of our work show that the presence of Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Mo in the alloy drives the critical pitting potential

layout_dets.text: electropositive. The Mo in the alloy was found to catalyze
